clue.text: Economise when importing old wine

indicators.note: a country importing goods takes them in, so the economising word takes the old letter inside it

parts.note: to economise is to save

explanation.surface: Someone tries to cut costs while still buying in vintage wine from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white Italian wine from the Veneto region near Verona.

clue.text: Bond creator elevated by Queen and head of government in turn

indicators.note: these pieces go in the turning word, inside it

parts.note: slue is a variant of slew, to turn or swing round
elevated means up
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sounds like the creator of James Bond being raised up by royalty and a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is not Ian Fleming's spy: it is the bond adhesive makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is a strong fast-setting adhesive that sticks surfaces together firmly.

clue.text: Island administered under Sark that's out of bounds?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits under the first
out of bounds means the word loses its boundary letters, first and last

parts.note: to run something is to administer it, so administered is ran

explanation.surface: Suggests an island governed under Sark's control is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island, which makes it tempting as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Draw out scandal involving fruit, with millions missing?

indicators.note: the fruit word is missing the millions letter

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
M is the abbreviation for million
a scandal involving something is named as that thing plus the suffix -gate, after Watergate, so this piece follows the fruit

explanation.surface: Wants to prolong a scandal about fruit in which millions disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: A scandal involving fruit would be dubbed fruit-gate, after Watergate, which is why the fruit comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen or stretch something, which is drawing it out.

clue.text: Set aside search in spot by river

indicators.note: the river letter is placed by, that is next to, the rest
the search word sits in the spotting word, enclosed by its letters

parts.note: to spot is to see
a quest is a search
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An instruction to put aside a search conducted at a particular place beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester something is to isolate it or remove it, keeping it apart from the rest.

clue.text: Colour in small gardens

parts.note: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: Describes some colour to be seen in compact gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Colour is a verb here, to distort or bias.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour a report is to slant or bias it, which is to skew it.

clue.text: Order to advance rapidly with intelligence over border

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: quick can mean clever, as in quick-witted
a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches

explanation.surface: A command to push forward fast, guided by intelligence reports, across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick march is a military drill command telling troops to march off at normal brisk pace.

clue.text: Waugh, for instance, gets name raised regularly

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means the name letter moves higher up the word

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh was the English novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist's name keeps being brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: EVELYN has its N moved up two places to come before the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means at a steady, uniform rate or spacing, as something regular is.

clue.text: Reserve has time to get out of condition before sport days

indicators.note: the first pair come before the sport and days pieces

parts.note: to rust is to deteriorate through lack of use
sport means fun, as in being in sport
D is the abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: A reserve player loses fitness ahead of a sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust fund is money held aside for someone, a financial reserve.

clue.text: Refuse to accept some dancing around piano

indicators.note: the dance word goes around the piano letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Declining to dance around a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack or offer is to fend it off or rebuff it.

clue.text: Some work penned by Chopin, say, is revolutionary for composer

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, as in a pen

parts.note: Chopin was Polish, so he is an example of a Pole
an erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a radical piece of music written by Chopin.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopin looks like the composer, but he is only there as an example of a Polish person; the composer is an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an eighteenth-century Italian composer, known for his Stabat Mater.

clue.text: Supply ecstasy and crack

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a wisecrack or quip

explanation.surface: Reads like a dealer offering ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to provide them with what they need, a synonym of supply as a verb.

clue.text: What degenerate keeps back to break an agreement

indicators.note: the kept letters run back, from right to left
the word degenerate keeps the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Asks what a corrupt person holds on to when going back on a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or deal, failing to honour what was undertaken.

clue.text: What might delay black grouse breeding, returning wasted

indicators.note: returning means the combined words are read back from the end

parts.note: running late is what might hold things up and delay them
leks are the display grounds where black grouse gather to breed

explanation.surface: Suggests something holding back the breeding season of black grouse, leaving them emaciated.
explanation.walkthrough: A lek is the communal display ground where male black grouse strut to attract mates; 'returning' turns the whole combined string round, not just one part.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasted, emaciated body is thin to the bone, described as skeletal.

clue.text: Cathedral pressure over what bishop wears in rich supply

indicators.note: in a down answer, the cathedral and pressure pieces sit over the ring

parts.note: Wells is a cathedral city in Somerset, England
P is the physics symbol for pressure
a bishop wears an episcopal ring

explanation.surface: Church politics: cathedral pressure over the bishop's regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is a fountainhead, an abundant source of something.

clue.text: Day at wheel travelling round to act as guide

indicators.note: letters travelling round move about and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A day spent at the wheel, driving round, to show others the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead the way is to go first and show others where to go, as a guide does.

clue.text: Did badly in fighting drug dependency

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the fighting word

parts.note: action means fighting, as in seeing action

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A soldier fared poorly in combat because of a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did badly' looks like the verdict on the fighting, but 'badly' only jumbles the three letters before 'in' puts them inside the fighting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Addiction is a compulsive dependence on a substance such as a drug.

clue.text: Yellowish-brown polish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is a pale yellowish-brown colour, like ... leather
second meaning: to polish a surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a light tan colour and the act of rubbing something until it shines.

clue.text: Strong alpha males? Beginning to think this is heavenly

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun, the heavenly vault

parts.note: firm means strong
A is the NATO alphabet letter alpha
men are males

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gym-goer's musing that macho types think themselves divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the sky or heavens, the vault of the heavens above.

clue.text: Poet cuts all that's irregular to keep uniform

indicators.note: the jumbled letters keep the uniform letter inside them
irregular means the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A poet trims every line that does not scan, to keep things consistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Catullus was a Roman lyric writer of the first century BC, famed for his verses to Lesbia.

clue.text: Bear not starting to move around

indicators.note: the bear word loses the letter it starts with

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A bear that is reluctant to begin walking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddies swirls in circles, so to eddy is to whirl about.

clue.text: TV comedy increasingly awful, some say? Want to cut it

indicators.note: the want word cuts into the other, splitting it open

parts.note: badder is a non-standard comparative of bad, used only by some speakers
want means lack

explanation.surface: A grumble that a TV comedy keeps getting worse and should be axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' flags that BADDER is not standard English, not that anything sounds like anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackadder was a BBC historical sitcom starring Rowan Atkinson, running in the 1980s.

clue.text: Flowery and fluid in speech

parts.note: fl. is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl. oz.
oral means spoken, in speech

explanation.surface: Describes an ornate, fluent way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means of or decorated with flowers, a synonym of flowery.

clue.text: Cooked Cape sole, cole and peas? This dish perhaps repeated

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh, worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe listing fish, cabbage and peas, served more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CAPE SOLE gives the answer; 'cole and peas' rearranges to the same letters, which is the dish 'repeated', a playful second helping of the same trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, flattened and fried, served as a dish.

clue.text: Brood raised outside south Surrey town

indicators.note: the turned word sits outside the south letter
in a down answer, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to brood is to mope
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Sulking about something happening south of here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MOPE into EPOM, which wraps round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a town in Surrey, England, home of the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Column holding aloft a rounded vault

indicators.note: the column abbreviation holds the aloft word inside it

parts.note: aloft means up

explanation.surface: A pillar that bears up a curved roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small dome, a rounded roof or ceiling over a building.

clue.text: Creature at one time seen round central part of Hindu Kush?

indicators.note: the time word is seen round the central letter, enclosing it

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: the middle letter of the nine letters of Hindu Kush

explanation.surface: An animal glimpsed once in the heart of the Hindu Kush mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Leis woven in Hawaii, perhaps

indicators.note: woven means the letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Flower garlands made by hand on Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii, the largest island of its archipelago, is an example of an island.

clue.text: Work-shy person — but not very — is one on a downward slope

indicators.note: but not means the very letter is excluded from the shirker

parts.note: a skiver is British slang for someone who dodges work

explanation.surface: Someone a bit lazy, though not extremely so, is on the way down.
explanation.walkthrough: A skiver, in British English, is someone who skips work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier slides down snowy mountain pistes, so is literally a person going downhill.

clue.text: Abuse individual in pub before church

indicators.note: the pub part comes before the church letters
the individual word goes in the pub word, enclosed by it

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole means single or individual
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone receives abuse in a pub on the way to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude and disrespectful talk, a form of verbal abuse or cheek.

clue.text: Grimace about denial set down in sermon, perhaps

indicators.note: the grimace word goes about the rest, wrapping around it

parts.note: a moue is a pout or grimace
no is a denial
to log is to record or set down in writing

explanation.surface: A face pulled at a refusal that has been written into a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one person, and a sermon is one example.

clue.text: Drained power during broadcast

indicators.note: the power letter comes during the broadcast word, within it

parts.note: something broadcast is sent out
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Electricity is used up during a transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means exhausted or used up, with no energy left, like a drained battery.
